name: Ryan Mcgovern
review:
**Fit summary:** Strong substance-use/recovery background; less alignment with the adolescent-specific and bilingual requirements.
**Strengths:** CRPA and CASAC-T credentials. Several years in recovery-coaching and MAT-program roles (Phoenix House, Central Nassau Guidance & Counseling, Oceanside Counseling Center) with crisis intervention and case management experience. Supervisory experience (DSP Assistant Manager).
**Gaps:** Background is adult SUD/recovery-focused rather than adolescent mental health. Spanish is listed as "Conversational," short of the full-fluency requirement.
**Consistency check:** Two food-service roles (Lead Line Cook and Prep Cook, both at Nassau Country Club) run concurrently with his full-time recovery-specialist roles for several years (2018-2026) — worth a clarifying phone-screen question about how these overlapped.
**Tenure/timeline notes:** None beyond the above.
**Recommendation:** Phone screen — solid recovery/SUD background; probe comfort with the adolescent population and the overlapping employment history.

name: Chelsea Walker
review:
**Fit summary:** Light-touch note for the general talent pool - directly relevant adolescent behavioral-health experience.
**Strengths:** Mental Health Technician on an adolescent behavioral health unit (monitoring, vitals, daily needs, structured/therapeutic environment); also a classroom assistant supporting students with behavioral/emotional needs.
**Gaps:** Work history dates aren't populated in the structured data, so tenure can't be assessed yet.
**Recommendation:** Keep warm - genuinely relevant adolescent BH background; worth matching to a BHT/MHT-type opening if one comes up, since there's no direct-care req open for her right now.

name: Brenda Iribarren
review:
**Fit summary:** Light-touch note for the general talent pool - fully bilingual with a strong intake/admissions background.
**Strengths:** Intake Counselor, Admissions Therapist, Lead Assessor, and Mental Health Therapist experience; fully bilingual English/Spanish; explicitly looking for remote, part-time work.
**Gaps:** Direct adolescent-specific experience is limited to early-career daycare/VPK work, not treatment-program intake with teens specifically.
**Recommendation:** Keep warm, but also worth a direct look against the open Licensed Clinical Intake Specialist and Mental Health Program Coordinator - Virtual reqs - her bilingual intake/admissions background is a closer functional match to both of those than to a general pool placement.

name: VICTORIA IORILLO
review:
**Fit summary:** Real admissions/healthcare-industry background, but not outreach/business-development experience specifically, plus a stated interest in moving toward younger populations that this adult-focused role doesn't offer.
**Strengths:** Admissions Coordinator in substance use/mental health treatment - understands admissions, referral relationships, and the client journey; came through an employee referral.
**Gaps:** No referral-source development, field-based territory management, or outreach/BD metrics in her history - her background is admissions coordination and medical-assistant work, not business development; Basic Spanish only; her own answer about why she's leaving her current role ("I've always wanted to work with younger ages... originally went to school for pediatric psych nurse") signals she may be looking for adolescent-focused work, while this role is adult substance use treatment - worth surfacing directly rather than assuming it away.
**Recommendation:** Hold/comment - genuine healthcare/admissions background, but both the core BD-experience gap and the stated interest in a different population are worth a direct conversation before investing further.

name: Alexis Bravo
review:
**Fit summary:** Reasonable match - education-program coordination background (an explicitly acceptable setting per the guide) and fluent Spanish, though comp expectations are on the low end and Florida residency isn't confirmed.
**Strengths:** Religious Education Program Coordinator managing curriculum and program operations; fluent bilingual; comp ask ($16-18/hr) fits the role's range.
**Gaps:** No behavioral-health, clinical, or community mental-health setting experience specifically (her educational setting is a faith-based program, not BH-adjacent); address doesn't confirm Florida residency [VERIFY].
**Consistency check:** None apparent.
**Recommendation:** Phone screen - solid program-coordination fundamentals and bilingual; confirm Florida residency and gauge comfort with a mental-health-specific caseload versus her faith-education background.

name: Anhia Santana
review:
**Fit summary:** Strong functional match - direct youth-behavioral-support experience across several relevant roles, though based in Pennsylvania rather than Florida.
**Strengths:** Therapeutic Staff Support (TSS) and Youth Behavior Specialist roles are directly analogous to supporting adolescents in a structured program; Truancy Case Manager and Instructional Assistant roles add case-coordination and school-system experience; fluent bilingual; comp ask ($19/hr) matches the role's upper range exactly.
**Gaps:** Address is Pennsylvania, not Florida - the guide requires Florida residency with a private home workspace; her stated reason for leaving ("I have the adequate experience") doesn't actually explain why she's leaving, which is worth a direct, neutral follow-up rather than reading into it.
**Consistency check:** None apparent beyond the vague leaving-reason answer above.
**Tenure/timeline notes:** Not assessable - work history dates aren't populated in the structured data.
**Recommendation:** Phone screen to confirm Florida relocation status first - if that resolves, her TSS/youth-specialist background is one of the closer functional matches in this pool.
